transcript.text:
Thank you all for flagging these issues. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I finalize the sequence:

1. Jon — Furnace 7's thermocouple calibration certificate expires before this production window. Recalibration takes exactly 2 hours and must be completed before we run anything.

4. Elena — The installed gas analyzer failed its bump test and must be replaced with the available spare before any run can proceed.

So the constraints are clear: R must run first due to the oxidation limit. The thermocouple recalibration (2 hours) and gas analyzer replacement must both be completed before we start R. After R, we'll need to sequence Q and P — and Q will need those 15 first-piece hardness tests completed and held before release, which may affect timing between Q and P.

Proposed sequence: R, then Q, then P.

Pre-startup requirements: (1) Complete thermocouple recalibration — 2 hours. (2) Replace gas analyzer with spare.

Does everyone agree with this sequence and the pre-startup requirements? If so, I'll record it and we can proceed with sign-offs from maintenance, quality, logistics, and process safety.
